mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen steadily for three consecutive weeks (-60.4 to -50.7), indicating a reopening momentum that should continue to push retail mobility higher over the next four weeks as consumer routines normalize incrementally.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved each week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days, despite the prior three-week upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen each week (-49.3 to -45.3), reflecting gradual return-to-office activity that generates incidental weekday retail and dining visits, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -49.3 to -45.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 2 weeks even though WORKPLACES continues its upward trajectory.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below 15 points (crossing a threshold indicating reduced home-confinement), households substitute at-home time for out-of-home retail and recreation visits within one week, raising RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 15.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 19.4 to 16.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following RESIDENTIAL crossing below 15.0, or RESIDENTIAL never crosses the threshold and RETAIL_REC still rises, invalidating the trigger specificity.

mechanism_narrative: A joint recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility (both trending upward together) signals restored commuting infrastructure use that compounds with retail recovery, producing a stronger RETAIL_REC increase than either series alone would predict, over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -60.0 to -55.1 and WORKPLACES rose from -49.3 to -45.3 concurrently
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 28 days is no greater than growth predicted by WORKPLACES alone, indicating no synergistic interaction between TRANSIT and WORKPLACES recovery.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS rebound in the most recent week (27.1 to 40.3) reflects increased outdoor recreation during summer, which typically substitutes for indoor retail visits, dampening or slowing the pace of RETAIL_REC recovery over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from 27.1 to 40.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise at the same or faster pace over the next 2 weeks despite elevated PARKS mobility, showing no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility were to fall more than 10 points week-on-week (a proxy for renewed mobility restrictions or public caution), it would signal a policy tightening regime that suppresses RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks regardless of current reopening momentum.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has only moved by small increments (under 5 points) week-on-week in the snapshot
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points in a week but RETAIL_REC does not subsequently decline over the next 4 weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines without any such TRANSIT drop.

mechanism_narrative: The deceleration in RETAIL_REC's week-on-week gains (from +5.5 points to +3.6 points most recently) combined with persistently depressed GROCERY_PHARM (flat near -17) suggests consumer caution is plateauing, limiting further RETAIL_REC gains and producing a flat-to-declining trend over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC week-on-week gains shrank from +5.5 to +3.6 while GROCERY_PHARM stayed flat around -17
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean by a margin comparable to or greater than the prior four-week trend, despite decelerating gains and flat GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime where WORKPLACES mobility has been monotonically increasing for four consecutive weeks, this sustained institutional-level mobility recovery acts as a leading indicator that retail establishments are also permitted expanded operations, driving RETAIL_REC higher within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose every week from -49.3 to -45.3 across the four-week snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week immediately following confirmation of four consecutive weeks of WORKPLACES increases.
